requirement: SPEC.md section 4, and the compatibility contract above
note: The first family of operations: create, set, clear and the two renames. A refused batch answers with the objects it was given rather than with what it had reached, so a case that refuses reads as the proof that nothing was written. A rename of a variable is the one that reaches furthest: the slot moves, and so do the trees of every formula that read it, the markers inside a text object, the address macros of a math source, and the target a copy carries outside the slot set. A forced delete rewrites every reference into the object it removes to a reference error and reports the addresses it rewrote, so the cases carry a reader, two readers of one object, and a range whose table goes. The two resizes move cell slots about and rewrite the addresses of every formula that named one, so the cases carry a formula reading a cell before the moved line, one reading a cell after it, one reading the line that goes, and a range straddling it. A size slot is checked apart from the resize, because a formula there would let evaluation decide how many cells a table declares. The port and source cases are the two operations that change the slot set from text an operator typed. A port and the value it holds land in one batch, because the moment an out port exists the integrity check demands the addresses it declares resolve, and a source is checked against the objects the batch has reached so it can name one the same batch creates. The last four operations close the inventory. A vertex delete and an explode each carry a forced and an unforced case, because an unforced one is refused with the reader named and a forced one rewrites that reference to a reference error and reports it.
